scope: Authored fixtures and public modern adapter/session interfaces only; these passes do not measure original data progress.

cases.source: OpenControl is the public cancellation token; MovieSession::invalidate must cancel the currently active operation when terminating. A coalesced same-revision Tick must not replace the sole owner handle to that token. 800ms is sufficient for the identical child/input after token-sharing correction (~300ms).
cases.limits: Two valid asynchronous Ticks through common API; current App timer gates one outstanding Tick, so this is not proof of normal GUI reproduction. Existing base had the same token replacement. Deliverable child now cooperates with TERM; timeouts retain unfinished PID without forced signals. Earlier seven process tests used the old close policy and do not validate a replacement safe-close implementation.

cases.source: External decoder shutdown must receive TERM independently of dispatch worker signal mask. Measured worker-spawned child blocked TERM/INT (1/1); POSIX_SPAWN_SETSIGMASK with empty mask fixes both to 0/0. Probe records the actual child mask and runner rejects blocked TERM/INT.
cases.limits: The 150ms natural-lifetime diagnostic confirms inheritance without requiring forced termination. A later cleanup policy must still preserve pending PID ownership and truthful resource state; that new policy is not yet in the supplied snapshot.

cases.source: MovieSession permitsExit requires completed close, resource zero and worker idle; independently check existence of the self child PID captured before first frame, after native test reports completion. Signal 0 is only an existence query; harness sends no termination signal. This catches dropped PID ownership that could otherwise fake resource-zero flags.
cases.limits: Only the self child PID is queried; original work policies and private fixes are covered, new main cleanup still requires separate replay.

legacy_process_checks: Seven earlier process probes passed on original close policy. Do not interpret those as acceptance of the new main safe-close implementation.
